title: helm(private): enhance values schema and init-hook templating for safer upgrades/rollbacks
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: Private (VPC/on-prem) Helm charts need safer upgrade/rollback behavior for customers running stateful components and custom values. This PR tightens the values schema, improves templating for init hooks, and adds deterministic guardrails so chart upgrades do not accidentally orphan resources or fail on rollback. The change bundle includes: 1) stronger values schema (CRD-like validation blocks in values.schema.json) to catch unsupported combinations (e.g. enabling persistent init-hooks + disabled pvc). 2) templating fixes for init job annotations and ownerReferences so jobs are correctly cleaned up during chart lifecycle operations. 3) upgrade/rollback compatibility logic to avoid replacing PV-backed StatefulSets without a migration plan; we default to a safe no-op when incompatible changes are detected and surface clear release_notes. 4) small docs and helm test updates. All changes focused on private/redwood-private Helm chart in redwood-private-installer. See related Linear tasks ENG-4021 (helm upgrade reliability) and ENG-4090 (init-hook ownership semantics).
commits: 4a7b3d2: feat(helm): add strict values.schema.json for private chart
8c9dbe1: fix(helm): use release annotation on init jobs to ensure cleanup
d3f1a92: refactor(helm): centralize templating helpers for pvc/ownerrefs
b2e7f4c: test(helm): add chart tests covering upgrade path scenarios
c5a9e11: docs(helm): document rollback behavior and required values
changes_summary:
- values.schema.json: added required/oneOf rules to disallow invalid combinations (initJobs.enabled=true requires pvc.enabled=true and storage.class set).
- templates/init-job.yaml: switched to use helm.sh/release annotation and explicit ownerReferences when pvc is managed by chart; added pre-delete hook semantics for safe cleanup.
- templates/_helpers.tpl: introduced helper functions for stable naming and ownerref generation to avoid drifting names across upgrades.
- statefulset.yaml: added checks to prevent spec.template changes that would replace PVs; emits helm hook warning when unsafe change detected.
- tests: added helm test manifest that simulates upgrade/rollback and asserts resources are cleaned up and PVs preserved.
review_comments: Liam Chen (review): Can we please avoid adding any new breaking validations without a migration path? Suggest adding a migration flag that gates enforcement for one release cycle.

Ava Martinez (author): Added a migration gate 'schema.enforceOnce' that must be explicitly set to true to hard-fail. By default the validator warns and emits a release_note. Updated tests to cover both behaviors.

Priya Kapoor (review): The init job ownerReferences look good, but please ensure we do not set ownerrefs when the PVC is external. Otherwise deletion will cascade.
Action: Added an explicit check and unit tests for external PVC scenario.

Marco Alvarez (review): CI lint failed on first run due to CRLF in values.schema.json — fixed. Also asked to add clearer release notes for operators.
Action: Updated CHANGELOG.md with operator-facing instructions and rollback checklist.
Priya Kapoor (approval): Approving; validated upgrade-path tests against a local k3s cluster.
merge_commit_message:
feat(helm): enhance values schema + init-hook templating for safer upgrades/rollbacks

Adds strict schema rules, templating helpers, ownerReference fixes, and upgrade/rollback tests. Migration gate 'schema.enforceOnce' added to avoid accidental breakage.
release_notes:
- Helm (private): enforce safer upgrade paths for PV-backed stateful workloads.
- Added values.schema.json validations to catch incompatible value combinations.
- Init jobs now use release annotations and ownerReferences when appropriate to ensure cleanup.
- Migration flag 'schema.enforceOnce' available to opt-in to strict validation for one release cycle. Operators: read CHANGELOG for rollback checklist.
post_merge_actions: Backport to release/2026-02 if customers report immediate upgrade regressions.
Coordinate with support (SUP-1287) to notify existing on-prem customers about optional migration flag.
Monitor canary upgrades for at least 72h and watch PV retention metrics in the Redwood Console.
